prompt.context: Your client is Mark Bellissimo, CEO of Wellington Equestrian Partners (WEP). Mark, a Harvard MBA with no background in the equestrian industry aside from watching his daughters ride at competitions, created WEP in 2006 with the mission of transforming Wellington, FL from a town with a large horse show to a community with a vibrant equestrian industry. As of now, Mark has succeeded in creating an incredible competition circuit in FL (called the Winter Equestrian Festival) and is seeking an investment from a reputable investment firm. In order to do so, he needs to 1. assess the total economic impact the festival has on the community each year, and 2. brainstorm ways to expand his business that the investor might be excited about. You have been asked to assist Mark with this analysis and with crafting a 60-second pitch, that includes expansion plans, for the outside investor. For context, top riders and trainers from around the world come to Wellington, FL for 12 weeks every winter to compete against elite competition and avoid the cold weather. You can think of this like you would any other sporting league/venue with on and off seasons.
prompt.question: What is the total annual economic impact of the Winter Equestrian Festival on the local community, and what expansion opportunities should Mark present to a prospective investor?

clarifying_info.q: How long does the festival run each year?
clarifying_info.a: The festival runs for 12 weeks (approximately 3 months), from January through April.

clarifying_info.q: How many exhibitors attend the festival?

clarifying_info.a: Up to 3,000 horses compete in any given week.

clarifying_info.q: What is the ticket price for spectators?
What are the stabling and care fees?

clarifying_info.a: $75 per entry; horses compete in approximately 5 entries per week.
$1,000 per exhibitor for 3 months; each exhibitor has one trainer.

clarifying_info.q: What is the hotel booking volume and rate?
clarifying_info.a: 120,000 hotel nights at approximately $150 per night.

clarifying_info.q: What do attendees spend at restaurants and shops?
clarifying_info.a: $1,000 per person over 3 months; approximately 15,000 people spending locally.

framework: Economic impact calculation: identify all revenue categories generated by the festival (competition revenues, spectator revenues, local hospitality revenues)
Competition revenues: entry fees, stabling/care fees, training fees, veterinary fees, miscellaneous equipment fees — analyze by horse or by exhibitor
Non-competition revenues: spectator tickets, hotel bookings, restaurants and retail spending
Quantify each category: identify quantity and unit price, then multiply to get totals
Expansion brainstorm: organize into internal strategies (venue/format changes) and external strategies (partnerships, media, geographic expansion)
Evaluation method for expansion: assess revenue potential, cost, risk, and timeline (short vs. long-term)
60-second pitch: combine economic impact figure with top expansion ideas, risks, and next steps

questions.prompt: Calculate the total annual economic impact of the Winter Equestrian Festival.
questions.guidance: Candidate should first brainstorm revenue categories (entry fees, coaching, stabling, equipment, spectators, hotels, retail) before asking for data. Unique-to-horses categories (vet fees, stabling) should be identified. Target answer is approximately $112.5 million. A well-reasoned estimate in the ballpark using many of the categories is acceptable.

math.setup: Sum all revenue streams: competition-related costs paid by exhibitors/horses, plus spectator and hospitality revenues.
steps: Overall competition spend: 15,000 exhibitors x $28,858 per party of 5.4 people = $80,161,111 (aggregate spend figure)
Stabling and care: 3,000 horses x $3,000/horse/month x 3 months = $27,000,000
Entry fees: 3,000 horses x 5 entries/horse/week x 12 weeks x $75/entry = $13,500,000
Veterinary fees: 3,000 horses x $2,000/horse over 3 months = $6,000,000
Miscellaneous equipment fees: 15,000 exhibitors x $1,000/exhibitor over 3 months = $15,000,000
Training fees: 15,000 exhibitors x 1 trainer each x $1,000/exhibitor over 3 months = $15,000,000
Restaurants and shopping: 15,000 people x $1,000/person over 3 months = $15,000,000

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm ways WEP can expand its business that would excite a potential investor. Organize your ideas and note risks.

categories.name: Internal strategies
ideas: Expand festival beyond 12 weeks — more weeks means more revenue; risk: loss of prestige
Offer multiple festivals outside the 12-week window — more revenue opportunities; risk: uncertain competitive landscape at other times of year
Repurpose venue for other events (concerts, other sports) during off-season; risk: expensive and potentially damaging to property
Increase number of exhibitors by enhancing venue quality and horse-friendly conditions; risk: expensive, may require higher entry fees
Increase spectator attendance by making the sport accessible (food, carnivals for kids, instructional pamphlets, parking, advertising); risk: uncertain uptake
Acquire more surrounding property to expand the venue; risk: acquisitions may not generate sufficient incremental profit

categories.name: External strategies
ideas: Partner with local hotels and tourism board to attract more out-of-town visitors; risk: increased traffic may not convert to festival revenue
Attract media attention (e.g., NBC Sports) to grow viewership and future participants; risk: viewership may be insufficient, potential reputational damage
Increase sponsorship from brands targeting equestrian demographics (e.g., Rolex, Fidelity Investments); risk: sport may appear too elite for average consumer
Partner with schools and riding academies to grow the sport's participant base; risk: target population will not compete at high level for many years
Incentivize other companies to promote the festival; risk: uncertain success rate
Expand to new geographic locations; risk: expensive, requires understanding of competitive landscape
Expand into adjacent industries; risk: WEP may lack qualifications

recommendation: The Winter Equestrian Festival contributes approximately $112.5 million annually to the local economy through competition, spectator, and hospitality revenue streams
WEP should pursue growth through multiple festivals throughout the year, deeper local community engagement to grow spectator attendance, and expansion to new locations to build market share
risks: Expensive expansion plans may not convert to incremental sales
Competitor response to multiple-festival format is uncertain
Extending the season or expanding geographically risks diluting the festival's prestige
next_steps: Assess market share potential and competitive landscape in candidate new locations
Survey current competitors and top riders on willingness to travel to Florida (or other venues) multiple times per year
Conduct cost-benefit analysis on venue improvements needed to increase exhibitor capacity
